Here we derive steady and beat sources together, separate detector curvature
from recurrent gain at a pinned Jansen--Rit (JR) operating point, and derive
the static-to-dynamic crossover in an exact QIF mean field. A head-model
illustration compares the resulting spatial maps, while equal-RMS carrier
controls distinguish beat-dependent modulation from induced oscillations.
after:
For weak static detection, beat and steady sources follow the carrier product
and summed squares, respectively. At a pinned Jansen--Rit (JR) operating point,
recurrent gain varies independently of detector curvature; fast-carrier steady
rectification in the QIF mean field follows the rate curve's slope even where curvature predicts
the opposite sign. In one head model, current-ratio changes move the envelope
and mean-square centroids oppositely while preserving the quadratic beat pattern.
Equal-RMS mean-field carrier controls show that the steady shift alone can
induce oscillations without a beat.

after:
The steady source provides a way for current-ratio changes to reshape the
beat response: it weights $\mathcal P_1^2$ and $\mathcal P_2^2$ by the squared
currents and can thereby shift the operating points. Such state changes fall
outside the fixed-state argument above. Threshold effects also depart from
the weak quadratic regime; the $2\min$ steering law requires envelope following.

The product law permits an interior beat maximum. Its spatial weighting also
depends on local detector and network factors (Eq.~\eqref{eq:receiver}), so
resonance can compensate for an unfavorable product only where the source
is nonzero.

is $0.12$, below the E-only Hopf threshold $\delta\eta_E^*\approx0.286$.

after:
At $\bar\eta=0.85$ and $A_f=10$, the original finite-cutoff run gives
beat depth $0.09$ and a $2.8\%$ mean-rate increase. Its quantitative depth
remains unconverged because of cutoff and population sensitivity (supplement,
\S\ref{app:qif-checks}--\ref{supp:theta-pilot}). The estimated rectified
E-drive shift remains below $\delta\eta_E^*$, the shift in excitatory drive
required to cross the Hopf while holding the inhibitory drive fixed.
At $\bar\eta=1.5$, the original finite-cutoff run gives a $42$~Hz depth
of about $0.02$ and a $1.6\%$ mean-rate increase, while ongoing gamma dominates.

The JR and QIF models demonstrate local mixing followed by recurrent
amplification. Applying these mechanisms to physiological kHz stimulation
requires calibration of membrane access and the generated source. The short-time
cases in Table~\ref{tab:doors} are access assumptions; varying the effective
membrane time quantifies their consequences. Cellular mixing \cite{mirzakhalili2020,luff2024mixer} and network
amplification \cite{caldas2024,karimi2024,esmaeilpour2021} have complementary
experimental and modeling support; their combined transfer remains unmeasured.
after:

amplification. Cellular mixing \cite{mirzakhalili2020,luff2024mixer} and network
amplification \cite{caldas2024,karimi2024,esmaeilpour2021} have complementary
experimental and modeling support, but their combined transfer at physiological
kHz fields remains unmeasured. The short-time cases in Table~\ref{tab:doors}

For comparison, the carrier-averaged, matched-peak, open-loop ratio has a
numerically estimated supremum of $0.348$ over bounded nondecreasing memoryless
transfers (supplement, \S\ref{app:bound}, Eq.~\eqref{eq:etasup}). A positive
mixture of step responses extends the logistic calculation to this class.
Approaching the bound requires a transition sharp relative to the input:
microvolt logistic widths at the illustrative polarizations. Its step-like
limit has a second-harmonic ratio near $0.15$, differing from weak square-law
and linear envelope detection. The bound excludes dynamic QIF and general
cellular mechanisms. Increasing a common matched polarization cannot exceed
it; unequal polarizations invalidate the matching. Unequal-current TI and
matched-depth AM-tACS comparisons do not measure this open-loop ratio.
after:
For balanced TI and a direct sinusoid matched in peak polarization at the
same operating point, the carrier-averaged open-loop fundamental-amplitude
ratio has a numerically estimated supremum of $0.348$ over bounded,
nondecreasing memoryless transfers (supplement, \S\ref{app:bound},
Eq.~\eqref{eq:etasup}). Dynamic QIF is outside this detector class.
